answer: A verifiable delay function (VDF) can gate entry: each new agent identity must compute a sequential proof that takes about two hours of single-threaded work before it can transact. Unlike ordinary proof-of-work, a VDF cannot be sped up by adding machines, so a Sybil farmer faces the same wall-clock cost per fake identity. Picture the network as a graph where every honest vertex is a willow rooted by that delay, while a comet of quickly spawned Sybils burns out before it can join. Attackers pay in time, and time cannot be parallelized.
